records.title: Effectiveness of an intensive outpatient treatment programme combining prolonged exposure and EMDR therapy for adolescents and young adults with PTSD in a naturalistic setting.
records.authors: Rentinck EM, van Mourik R, de Jongh A, Matthijssen SJMA.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Publication identity and reported study design checked. Outcome blinding is not established in the material reviewed; no single- or double-blind RCT classification is assigned.

records.finding: A six-day programme combining prolonged exposure, EMDR, physical activity and support from relatives or friends included 74 people aged 12–25. At one month, 65% no longer met PTSD criteria; dropout was 4%.
records.limitation: Intensive clinician-delivered, multimodal treatment with no randomized comparator. The sample included 36 people aged 12–17 and 38 aged 18–25; it does not establish a gentle entertainment effect.

evidence.relationshipNote: Intensive clinician-delivered, multimodal treatment with no randomized comparator. The sample included 36 people aged 12–17 and 38 aged 18–25; it does not establish a gentle entertainment effect.

records.title: The effect of eye movement desensitization and reprocessing-based online group counseling for university students: Psychological need satisfaction, psychological resilience, psychological well-being, and small 't' trauma.
records.journal: Psychological trauma : theory, research, practice and policy
records.authors: Yilmaz Dinç S, Sapmaz F.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Publication identity and reported study design checked. Outcome blinding is not established in the material reviewed; no single- or double-blind RCT classification is assigned.

records.finding: EMDR-based online group counselling for university students reported improvements in psychological need satisfaction, resilience, wellbeing and several small-t trauma measures across repeated assessments.
records.limitation: University enrolment does not establish an exclusively 18–24 sample. The abstract does not provide sufficient age or masking detail; body-sense effects were not significant.

evidence.relationshipNote: University enrolment does not establish an exclusively 18–24 sample. The abstract does not provide sufficient age or masking detail; body-sense effects were not significant.

records.title: Peer-delivered combined EMD and imagery rescripting for traumatized Chinese university students: a RCT.
records.authors: Fan H, Zhang J, Wang Y, Yang K, Wang Y, Yang X.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The study describes an open-label randomized design. Participants reported their own outcomes; hypothesis masking and blinded analysis do not establish masked outcome collection.

records.finding: Ninety-five university students were randomized to peer-delivered EMD plus imagery rescripting, imagery rescripting alone or care as usual. Four supervised sessions produced similar changes in depression and anxiety across groups; the combined intervention better maintained resilience gains at follow-up.
records.limitation: Trained peers received clinical supervision. The trial tested a combined intervention, with no significant group-by-time effects for depression, anxiety or self-efficacy.

evidence.relationshipNote: Trained peers received clinical supervision. The trial tested a combined intervention, with no significant group-by-time effects for depression, anxiety or self-efficacy.

records.title: Brief psychological intervention with traumatized young women: the efficacy of eye movement desensitization and reprocessing.
records.authors: Scheck MM, Schaeffer JA, Gillette C.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Publication identity and reported study design checked. Outcome blinding is not established in the material reviewed; no single- or double-blind RCT classification is assigned.

records.finding: Sixty women aged 16–25 received two sessions of EMDR or active listening. Both groups improved, with larger immediate changes in the EMDR group.
records.limitation: A small, early trial with a mixed adolescent/young-adult sample. Immediate outcomes do not establish durable effects or an exclusively 18–24 result.

evidence.relationshipNote: A small, early trial with a mixed adolescent/young-adult sample. Immediate outcomes do not establish durable effects or an exclusively 18–24 result.

records.title: Inflammation-related microRNAs are involved in stressful life events exposure and in trauma-focused psychotherapy in treatment-resistant depressed patients.
records.authors: Maffioletti E, Bocchio-Chiavetto L, Perusi G, Carvalho Silva R, Sacco C, Bazzanella R, Zampieri E, Bortolomasi M, Gennarelli M, Minelli A.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

records.finding: Blood microRNA was measured in 41 people with treatment-resistant depression; 21 received EMDR or trauma-focused CBT. miR-15a, miR-29a, miR-126, miR-195 and let-7f changed during treatment; baseline miR-29a was associated with response.
records.limitation: The longitudinal group combined 12 EMDR and nine CBT participants. This cohort also informs the 2023 stress-gene paper, so the two publications are not independent replications.

evidence.relationshipNote: The longitudinal group combined 12 EMDR and nine CBT participants. This cohort also informs the 2023 stress-gene paper, so the two publications are not independent replications.

records.title: MicroRNAs expression changes associated with trauma-focused psychotherapy efficacy in treatment-resistant depression: An exploratory study.
records.authors: Buson L, Carvalho Silva R, Galbiati C, Bortolomasi M, Scaglia M, Perusi G, Abate M, Maffioletti E, Gennarelli M, Lorenzon N, Dierssen M, European College of Neuropsychopharmacology (ECNP) Pharmacogenomics & Transcriptomics Network, Minelli A.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

records.finding: In 24 people receiving EMDR or trauma-focused CBT for treatment-resistant depression, 148 microRNAs passed quality control. The combined sample’s miR-132-3p change survived correction for multiple testing.
records.limitation: EMDR-only subgroup changes did not survive multiple-testing correction. The result does not establish an EMDR-specific microRNA effect.

evidence.relationshipNote: EMDR-only subgroup changes did not survive multiple-testing correction. The result does not establish an EMDR-specific microRNA effect.

records.title: DNA methylation changes in association with trauma-focused psychotherapy efficacy in treatment-resistant depression patients: a prospective longitudinal study.
records.authors: Carvalho Silva R, Martini P, Hohoff C, Mattevi S, Bortolomasi M, Menesello V, Gennarelli M, Baune BT, Minelli A.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

records.finding: Blood DNA methylation was studied in 30 people with treatment-resistant depression receiving EMDR (18) or trauma-focused CBT (12). Differentially methylated regions included inflammation-related genes and pathways.
records.limitation: Small treatment groups and concurrent usual care limit attribution. DNA methylation is a separate measurement from RNA expression.

evidence.relationshipNote: Small treatment groups and concurrent usual care limit attribution. DNA methylation is a separate measurement from RNA expression.

records.title: Distinct saliva DNA methylation profiles in relation to treatment outcome in youth with posttraumatic stress disorder.
records.authors: Ensink JBM, Henneman P, Venema A, Zantvoord JB, den Kelder RO, Mannens MMAM, Lindauer RJL.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

records.finding: The study included 46 young people with PTSD and 41 trauma-exposed controls, aged 8–18. Saliva DNA-methylation differences associated with treatment response included C18orf63 and the stress-related CRHR2 locus.
records.limitation: Treatment combined evidence from EMDR and trauma-focused CBT. Saliva findings do not establish a brain-tissue effect or isolate eye movements.

evidence.relationshipNote: Treatment combined evidence from EMDR and trauma-focused CBT. Saliva findings do not establish a brain-tissue effect or isolate eye movements.

records.title: Epigenetic impact of a 1-week intensive multimodal group program for adolescents with multiple adverse childhood experiences.
records.authors: Kaliman P, Cosín-Tomás M, Madrid A, Roque López S, Llanez-Anaya E, Papale LA, Alisch RS, Davidson RJ.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: The methods report random-number allocation for 44 girls. Post-allocation participant or assessor masking is not established. The intervention combines mindfulness, art and group EMDR.

records.finding: A one-week programme combining mindfulness, artistic expression and EMDR group therapy studied 44 adolescent girls with multiple adverse experiences. Forty-nine DNA-methylation loci differed with intervention; SIRT5 and TRAPPC2L changes correlated with trauma measures.
records.limitation: The programme has several components. Saliva methylation findings do not isolate EMDR; the study detected no intervention effect on intrinsic epigenetic age acceleration.

evidence.relationshipNote: The programme has several components. Saliva methylation findings do not isolate EMDR; the study detected no intervention effect on intrinsic epigenetic age acceleration.

records.title: Successful treatment of post-traumatic stress disorder reverses DNA methylation marks.
records.authors: Vinkers CH, Geuze E, van Rooij SJH, Kennis M, Schür RR, Nispeling DM, Smith AK, Nievergelt CM, Uddin M, Rutten BPF, Vermetten E, Boks MP.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

records.finding: In veterans receiving trauma-focused psychotherapy, remission was associated with changes in 12 blood DNA-methylation regions. ZFP57 also showed evidence in an independent prospective deployment cohort.
records.limitation: Treatment included trauma-focused CBT and/or EMDR. This observational analysis does not isolate EMDR or establish altered gene expression from methylation alone.

evidence.relationshipNote: Treatment included trauma-focused CBT and/or EMDR. This observational analysis does not isolate EMDR or establish altered gene expression from methylation alone.

records.title: Pretreatment cortisol predicts trauma-focused psychotherapy response in youth with (partial) posttraumatic stress disorder.
records.authors: Zantvoord JB, Ensink JBM, Op den Kelder R, Wessel AMA, Lok A, Lindauer RJL.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

records.finding: Among 53 young people aged 8–18 treated with EMDR or trauma-focused CBT, higher pretreatment basal salivary cortisol was associated with greater subsequent symptom improvement.
records.limitation: The trauma script rarely produced a cortisol stress response. The predictive contribution was limited and insufficient for clinical application; this is not a gene-expression measurement.

evidence.relationshipNote: The trauma script rarely produced a cortisol stress response. The predictive contribution was limited and insufficient for clinical application; this is not a gene-expression measurement.

records.title: The Role of the Endocannabinoids 2-AG and Anandamide in Clinical Symptoms and Treatment Outcome in Veterans with PTSD.
records.authors: Leen NA, de Weijer AD, van Rooij SJH, Kennis M, Baas JMP, Geuze E.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Molecular or biomarker analysis with combined trauma-focused treatment exposure. No independently verified single- or double-blind randomized molecular comparison is assigned.

records.finding: Plasma anandamide and 2-AG were measured in 54 veterans with PTSD and 26 combat controls. Pretreatment levels did not predict symptom reduction following trauma-focused therapy; cortisol decreased over time.
records.limitation: Treatments included CBT with exposure or EMDR. Exploratory correlations require replication; endocannabinoid concentrations are distinct from gene expression.

evidence.relationshipNote: Treatments included CBT with exposure or EMDR. Exploratory correlations require replication; endocannabinoid concentrations are distinct from gene expression.

records.title: Stress and stress reactivity in posttraumatic stress disorder (PTSD) following eye movement desensitization (EMD): A randomized controlled trial.
records.journal: Journal of behavior therapy and experimental psychiatry
records.authors: Susanty E, Sijbrandij M, van der Mee DJ, Srisayekti W, Suparman Y, Huizink AC.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Publication identity and reported study design checked. Outcome blinding is not established in the material reviewed; no single- or double-blind RCT classification is assigned.

records.finding: Ninety-one adults with PTSD received eye-movement desensitization or memory retrieval alone. Both groups showed reduced stress reactivity; the study found no specific overall benefit of eye movements and inconsistent cortisol differences.
records.limitation: Saliva timing depended on participant adherence. This is the same registered component trial as the 2024 neurocognitive report, not an independent replication.

evidence.relationshipNote: Saliva timing depended on participant adherence. This is the same registered component trial as the 2024 neurocognitive report, not an independent replication.

records.title: Transcriptional Modulation of Stress-Related Genes in Association with Early Life Stress Exposure and Trauma-Focused Psychotherapy in Treatment-Resistant Depression Patients
records.journal: Journal of EMDR Practice and Research
records.authors: Rosana Carvalho Silva; Vincenzo Dattilo; Giulia Perusi; Monica Mazzelli; Elisabetta Maffioletti; Roberta Bazzanella; Marco Bortolomasi; Annamaria Cattaneo; Massimo Gennarelli; Alessandra Minelli

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Longitudinal observational molecular analysis of a combined EMDR/TF-CBT cohort. No randomized masked molecular comparison.

records.finding: In 21 people receiving EMDR or trauma-focused CBT for treatment-resistant depression, whole-blood NR3C1, FKBP5 and SGK1 expression varied over time. FKBP5 and SGK1 fell significantly at eight weeks; transcript levels rebounded during follow-up.
records.limitation: EMDR and CBT participants were analysed together, alongside medication. The 2021 microRNA paper uses the same underlying cohort; this is not an independent replication or evidence of an isolated eye-movement effect.

evidence.intervention: 24 sessions of EMDR or trauma-focused CBT alongside usual medication
evidence.relationshipNote: Combined therapy cohort; no untreated molecular comparator.

records.title: The photoreceptor mosaic
records.authors: P K Ahnelt
records.design: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic
records.summary: Ahnelt describes how human rods and cones are distributed across the retina. Cone packing is especially dense near the fovea; different cone populations have different arrangements. This provides biological context for exploring local packing and sampling geometry in Vision Atlas.
records.finding: Ahnelt describes how human rods and cones are distributed across the retina. Cone packing is especially dense near the fovea; different cone populations have different arrangements. This provides biological context for exploring local packing and sampling geometry in Vision Atlas.
records.limitation: The review does not demonstrate a universal perfect hexagonal retina, tetrahedral visual processing, or a Fibonacci mechanism. It is anatomical evidence, not an EMDR treatment trial or a quantum-stability experiment.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.evidenceType: Anatomical review of the human retinal photoreceptor mosaic
evidence.measurement: Spatial sampling by retinal photoreceptor populations.
evidence.relationshipNote: Compare the Atlas geometry with measured local packing, density and irregularity; retain the differences between retinal regions.
evidence.reviewDepth: Publisher or author abstract and bibliographic metadata; selected explanatory sections where available.
evidence.hypothesisBoundary: Connections to M9 P24, Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Epsilon remain research hypotheses. Shared geometry does not establish a shared physical mechanism.

jadad.reason: Not a human randomised clinical trial.

records.title: Retinal origin of orientation maps in visual cortex
records.authors: Se-Bum Paik; Dario L Ringach
records.design: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations
records.summary: Paik and Ringach propose that interference between regularly spaced ON- and OFF-centre retinal ganglion-cell mosaics helps form orientation maps in visual cortex. Their model predicts hexagonal organisation of orientation-domain centres, with supporting patterns reported in four mammalian species.
records.finding: Paik and Ringach propose that interference between regularly spaced ON- and OFF-centre retinal ganglion-cell mosaics helps form orientation maps in visual cortex. Their model predicts hexagonal organisation of orientation-domain centres, with supporting patterns reported in four mammalian species.
records.limitation: This is a proposed developmental mechanism with supporting observations. It does not establish that all visual cortex follows this model, that humans prefer hexagons, or that retinal geometry stabilises quantum information.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.evidenceType: Computational model with comparative visual-cortex observations
evidence.measurement: Moiré interference between two spatial mosaics.
evidence.relationshipNote: Test whether similar interference mathematics generates useful candidate patterns in the Atlas, then evaluate each physical system separately.
evidence.reviewDepth: Publisher or author abstract and bibliographic metadata; selected explanatory sections where available.
evidence.hypothesisBoundary: Connections to M9 P24, Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Epsilon remain research hypotheses. Shared geometry does not establish a shared physical mechanism.

jadad.reason: Not a human randomised clinical trial.

records.title: Hexadirectional coding of visual space in human entorhinal cortex
records.authors: Matthias Nau; Tobias Navarro Schröder; Jacob L. S. Bellmund; Christian F. Doeller
records.design: Human fMRI during controlled visual tracking
records.summary: Nau and colleagues found a sixfold directional pattern in human entorhinal-cortex activity during a visual tracking task. The result supports a grid-like representation of visual space and gives Vision Atlas a measured example of sixfold organisation in brain activity.
records.finding: Nau and colleagues found a sixfold directional pattern in human entorhinal-cortex activity during a visual tracking task. The result supports a grid-like representation of visual space and gives Vision Atlas a measured example of sixfold organisation in brain activity.
records.limitation: An fMRI population signal is not a direct image of individual grid cells or proof of a tetrahedral eye mechanism. This study does not test Fibonacci sequences, EMDR outcomes, or quantum error correction.

studyDesignAssessment.basis: Human fMRI during controlled visual tracking. This is not a clinical efficacy trial.

evidence.evidenceType: Human fMRI during controlled visual tracking
evidence.measurement: Sixfold rotational modulation of a population-level neural signal with gaze direction.
evidence.relationshipNote: Use explicit rotational-symmetry tests with competing periodicities and independent data, rather than judging a pattern by visual resemblance.
evidence.reviewDepth: Publisher or author abstract and bibliographic metadata; selected explanatory sections where available.
evidence.hypothesisBoundary: Connections to M9 P24, Alpha, Beta, Gamma and Epsilon remain research hypotheses. Shared geometry does not establish a shared physical mechanism.

jadad.reason: Not a human randomised clinical trial.
